nonLabourLines.description: Legacy Oracle migration tooling / read-replica access
Contingency for infrastructure (staging/CI runners, observability tooling)

assumptions: The provided rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: a single undifferentiated 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE available. No real team composition (e.g. separate BE/FE/QA/PM roles) or differentiated rates has been defined yet, so this estimate is indicative only and must be revised once actual roles and rates are assigned.

Effort was sized using a standard planning-poker conversion of ~8 hours per story point, adjusted per task for known complexity/risk (e.g. legacy data migration and payment integration weighted up; smaller UI tasks weighted at or below baseline). Total backlog is 172 points, translating to roughly 2,320 hours of work.

Only 1 FTE ('Team member') is currently staffed against this backlog. At 2,320 hours of estimated work, this single person would need approximately 58 weeks of full-time effort (at 40 hrs/week) to deliver the full backlog alone — the role is staffed far too thinly for the scope described. Either headcount must increase, timeline must extend substantially, or scope must be cut (see reductions).

No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; all effort and cost figures are estimates based on backlog descriptions and standard delivery norms, not on observed team velocity or past spend.

Non-labour costs are indicative placeholders for third-party services (Stripe fees/sandbox, Oracle migration tooling/read-replica access, an external WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit, and general staging/CI/observability infrastructure contingency).

Scenario spread (10th/50th/90th percentile) reflects uncertainty inherent in a single-FTE, placeholder-rate estimate: low case assumes some tasks (esp. legacy migration, multi-currency) go smoother than expected; high case assumes the usual overruns on integration-heavy and data-migration work plus review/QA cycles not separately staffed.

No dedicated QA, design, DevOps, or PM roles exist on the rate card, so all analysis, coding, testing, and deployment work is bundled into the single 'Team member' role's hours; quality and delivery risk is correspondingly higher than a properly staffed team.

Priority breakdown totals are derived by allocating each task's estimated labour cost (at $75/hr) by its stated backlog priority; non-labour costs are apportioned to the priority of the task they most directly support (e.g. Oracle tooling to High-priority PW-8, Stripe fees to Urgent-priority PW-7, accessibility audit and infra contingency split across Medium/Low).
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 172 story points across 24 tasks. Using ~8 hours/point as a baseline and adjusting per-task for known risk (payment integration, legacy migration, multi-currency, RBAC weighted up; simpler UI/config tasks weighted down), total effort comes to ~2,320 hours. With only one 'Team member' role available at $75/hr on a placeholder rate card, labour cost is 2,320 x $75 = $174,000. Non-labour costs of $5,500 cover Stripe setup, Oracle migration tooling, an external accessibility audit, and general infra contingency, bringing the most-likely total to $179,500. Low/high scenarios (10th/90th percentile) were built by applying roughly -16%/+30% swings to reflect the high uncertainty from single-FTE staffing, unproven velocity (no historical actuals), and the inherent risk in data-migration and payment-integration work. Priority breakdown allocates labour+non-labour cost by each task's stated priority. Because a single FTE cannot realistically deliver 2,320 hours of work in a normal timeframe, we flag this explicitly as a staffing gap requiring either more headcount, a much longer timeline, or backlog descoping — see reductions for concrete descope/defer options to bring cost and duration down.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 Admin back-office for support staff (Low priority, 13 points, internal-only tooling) from this phase
reductions.effect: Removes ~104 hours of build for an internal tool that does not affect customer-facing launch; support staff can continue using existing manual processes short-term.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 Usage analytics and reporting and PW-23 Contract tests against helpdesk API (both Low priority) to a post-launch phase
reductions.effect: Removes ~104 hours combined; analytics/CSV export and helpdesk contract tests are valuable but not required for initial go-live and can be delivered in a fast-follow release.

reductions.description: Defer PW-14 Multi-currency support (Medium, 13 points) until after initial launch, shipping USD-only first
reductions.effect: Removes ~130 hours; most SaaS portals can launch single-currency and add FX/settlement complexity once core flows are proven in production.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-8 Legacy data migration scope for phase 1 to a dry-run + subset migration (e.g. active accounts only) rather than full 400k/2M record cutover
reductions.effect: Cuts ~160 hours by narrowing initial migration scope; full historical backfill can run as a background job after go-live, reducing risk of a big-bang cutover.

reductions.description: Defer non-labour spend on the third-party WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit until after the accessibility pass (PW-15) is code-complete
reductions.effect: Avoids paying for an external audit before internal remediation work is finished; audit can be rebooked once the team believes the screens are compliant, avoiding wasted re-audit fees.

reductions.description: Staff a second 'Team member' FTE instead of stretching one person across 2,320 hours (~58 weeks) on a serial timeline
reductions.effect: This is not a direct cost saving but a scope/timeline risk mitigation: doubling headcount halves calendar time to roughly 29 weeks for the same total labour cost, reducing schedule risk and delayed-delivery costs not captured in this estimate.
